text: Not a bug on our side. No configuration of the Tinker OAI endpoint constrains the decode. response_format (both json_object and json_schema, with and without strict/name), vLLM guided_json, guided_decoding_backend, structured_outputs, nvext and extra_body nesting are all accepted with HTTP 200 and all produce output statistically indistinguishable from sending no parameter at all (the none control matches every mechanism, in both Part 2 and Part 3). Two invalid controls are also accepted, proving the field is never parsed. The native SDK has no such surface either. Do not send these parameters expecting effect.

tag: unenforced, but conforms well when prompted with the schema
text: 20/20 strictly-parseable JSON and 19/20 schema-valid + coverage-valid under the study's real prompt on a short contract. Under an adversarial prompt that invites prose, 8–10/10 fenced and 0/10 strictly parseable — identical to the no-parameter control. Conformance is a property of the prompt, not of any server-side enforcement. Its distinctive failure is reasoning overflow: with a fence-inviting prompt it returned empty content in 1–4 of 10 samples per mechanism.

tag: unenforced — the previous "json_object honored" note is WRONG
text: 20/20 strictly-parseable, schema-valid and coverage-valid under the study's real prompt — the best of the three — but that is voluntary compliance, not enforcement. Under the adversarial prompt it emitted a markdown fence on 10/10 samples with response_format: {"type": "json_object"} set, identical to the control. The structured_output: "json_object" entry in TINKER_MODEL_FACTS and the matching claim in plans/component-contracts.md are falsified and must be corrected to prompt_only. It is the only model that emits tool calls at all (17/20 under a forced named tool), but even then tool_choice is not honoured — it declines 3 times in 20.
